ObjectName.value: BLAAFARVEVÆRKET (Cobalt Works Blue pigment factory koboltmalm 1773-1893) museum Kunstgalleri Modum NORWAY 2025-08-13 ANGELUS by STEPHAN SINDING 1913 (bronze sculpture to Værket 2001) Glasshytten glass smeltery 1779 bindingsverk

Categories.value: Blaafarveværket|Self-published work|Timber buildings in Norway|Works of Stephan Sinding|Norway photographs taken on 2025-08-13

ImageDescription.value:
“Angelus” modeled in 1913 by Stephan Sinding (1846–1922). Cast in bronze for the Blaafarveværket collection in 2001. In the background: The Glasshytten glass smeltery originally built in 1779.
  • Blaafarveværket (Modum Blaafarveværk), or the 'Blue Colour Works', was a mining and industrial company in Modum, Norway, operating from 1776 to 1898. In the early 19th century it was Norway’s largest mining enterprise. The works extracted cobalt ore and produced blue pigment (smalt and cobalt blue), with a glasshouse for preparing cobalt glass that was ground into pigment powder. At its peak in the 1830s–40s the company supplied up to 80% of the world market for cobalt blue.
Since 1971, Blaafarveværket has been preserved as an open-air industrial museum museum and art gallery, with buildings, park, exhibitions, and mines, partially recreated as a mining environment as it appeared around 1840.
